content:
The Calendar & Clocks chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Calendar & Clocks tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Calendar & Clocks

Odd days and finding the day of the week, leap-year rules, and the angle between clock hands.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Ordinary year = 1 odd day, leap year = 2; 100 years = 5, 400 years = 0.
  • Angle between hands = |30H − 5.5M| degrees.
  • Hands coincide every 65 5⁄11 minutes (22 times in 12 h).
  • Minute hand 6°/min, hour hand 0.5°/min.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Treating century years as leap years (only ÷400 are).
  • Forgetting the 5.5M term in the hand-angle formula.
  • Miscounting odd days.
